slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /ɪ/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /ɪ/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hesitation or imprecise production of /ɪ/.

slides.expected_response: Students produce /p/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /p/, students repeat three times, then recheck.

slides.teacher_cue: Quick review — sight word. Say it as a whole unit. Use it in a sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students say I immediately without blending.
slides.correction_move: Model I in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hesitation or blending attempts — sight word should be instant recognition.

slides.teacher_cue: Play tin once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write tin accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay tin once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students encode tin accurately from sound to print.

slides.teacher_cue: Play pan once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write pan accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay pan once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students encode pan accurately from sound to print.

slides.teacher_cue: Play nap once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write nap accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay nap once, segment orally, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students encode nap accurately from sound to print.

slides.teacher_cue: New sound. The back of the tongue rises to touch the soft palate at the back of the mouth. Release with a burst — no voicing. Two spellings, one sound: c and k.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /k/ cleanly and understand that c and k represent the same sound.
slides.correction_move: Model /k/ with a hand at the throat confirming no vibration, then show both c and k cards. Students produce the sound from each.
slides.observation_note: Watch for confusion between c and k spellings, and for any voiced /g/ substitution.

slides.slide_title: Say c and k In Words
slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect c and k to one strong word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students say c and k clearly and connect it to a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Use can in a short oral sentence — I can tap. Say the word, then reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say can orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model can orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students produce a clean /k/ onset.

slides.teacher_cue: Say cat orally — a familiar animal. Reveal print and blend all three sounds.
slides.expected_response: Students say cat orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model cat orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students produce the short /æ/ clearly in this high-frequency word.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to a cap or mime putting one on. Say the word, then reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say cap orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model cap orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the final /p/ — students must close lips completely.

slides.teacher_cue: Explain a kit as a set of tools. Note: this word uses k not c. Say the word, reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say kit orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model kit orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students recognise k as the same sound as c.

slides.teacher_cue: Draw a tick mark. Say tick orally, then reveal print and blend. ck is one unit — both letters, one sound /k/.
slides.expected_response: Students say tick orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model tick orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat ck as a single unit and hold the short /ɪ/.

slides.teacher_cue: Mime picking something up. Say pick orally, then reveal print and blend. ck is one unit — same as tick.
slides.expected_response: Students say pick orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model pick orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for confusion of pick and tick — same vowel and coda unit ck, different onset.

slides.teacher_cue: Vocabulary warm-up. Say the word, connect meaning, then read it together.
slides.expected_response: Students read sick accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the word, then repeat chorally and point to each part if needed.
slides.observation_note: Watch for smooth oral reading before it appears in connected text.

slides.slide_title: Review c and k With Known Words
slides.teacher_cue: Read it, track the parts, and confirm that every part fits the taught pool for c and k.
slides.expected_response: Students read the word accurately and explain why it is safe to read.
slides.correction_move: Tap each sound or chunk, blend, then reread smoothly.
slides.observation_note: Use this as confidence-building cumulative review, not as a surprise challenge.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build cat left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build cat correctly: c | a | t.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of cat, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place every sound correctly, especially the target phoneme.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build cap left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build cap correctly: c | a | p.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of cap, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place every sound correctly, especially the target phoneme.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build tick left to right. ck goes together in one slot.
slides.expected_response: Students build tick correctly: t | i | ck.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of tick, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place ck as a single unit, not as separate c and k.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build pick left to right. ck goes together in one slot — same as tick.
slides.expected_response: Students build pick correctly: p | i | ck.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of pick, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place ck as a single unit in the coda position.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build kick left to right. k | i | ck — both ck letters go in the last slot.
slides.expected_response: Students build kick correctly: k | i | ck.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of kick, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat ck as a single unit and notice the k onset matches the ck coda — different spellings, same sound.

slides.teacher_cue: A is a sight word. cat and sat are decodable. Blend through each one left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students read "A cat sat." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can blend cat correctly using the new /k/ sound.

slides.teacher_cue: A and a are sight words. All other words are decodable. Read the full sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students read "I can pat a cat." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hold a five-word sentence in working memory.

content_payload.text_content: The cat can sit. A cat is in a cap.

slides.teacher_cue: Two sentences. The and I are sight words. All other words decodable.
slides.expected_response: Students read "The cat can sit. A cat is in a cap." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students read both sentences in sequence and produce /k/ cleanly in can, pick.

slides.slide_title: Read And Explain c and k

content_payload.text_content: The cat can sit. A cat is in a cap.
content_payload.comprehension_prompt: What does this tell you about the lesson words? Say it back in your own words.

slides.teacher_cue: Read it smoothly, then explain the c and k idea in your own words.
slides.expected_response: Students read accurately and explain the meaning of the c and k sentence.
slides.correction_move: Reread in a phrase, then prompt for a brief retell or answer.
slides.observation_note: Push comprehension right after decoding so the focus does not stay mechanical.

content_payload.text_content:

slides.teacher_cue: Echo read first, then students read chorally. Point to each word. Ask the comprehension prompt after.
slides.expected_response: Students read all sentences accurately and answer the comprehension prompt.
slides.correction_move: Echo read line by line, then support each sentence before rereading the full passage.
slides.observation_note: Watch for tracking accuracy and any phoneme production errors throughout.

slides.expected_response: Students reread with smoother phrasing and produce one oral sentence using a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Echo read one line at a time, then reread the full text and prompt one supported oral sentence.
slides.observation_note: Watch for improved fluency, accurate tracking, and whether students can transfer one lesson word into a new sentence.

slides.slide_title: Write c and k And Read Back

content_payload.prompt_text: Write the c and k target from memory. Then read it back and check every part.

slides.teacher_cue: Write the c and k target carefully from memory, then read it back aloud and check every part.
slides.expected_response: Students write accurately and read back what they wrote.
slides.correction_move: Prompt students to say each sound or chunk as they check their writing.
slides.observation_note: The goal is accurate encoding plus immediate self-checking.

content_payload.support_text: What changed? Same onset, different ending — what is different?

slides.teacher_cue: Read the words aloud. Ask: What changed? Same onset, different ending — what is different?
slides.expected_response: Students identify what changed and name the difference.
slides.correction_move: Model both words, isolate the changing part, then ask again.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hear and name the specific change.

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Read the model sentence. Then say a new sentence with one lesson word.

slides.teacher_cue: Use the model sentence once, then ask students to say a new sentence that keeps one lesson word but changes the meaning.
slides.expected_response: Students read the model sentence and say one new oral sentence using a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model one new sentence aloud, then have students repeat and generate their own.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hold the target pattern while generating a meaningful new sentence.

slides.slide_title: Use c and k In New Speech

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Say one sentence using c and k, then say a second sentence with one change.

slides.teacher_cue: Use c and k in one full sentence. Then change one part and say a second sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students produce one complete sentence and then extend or vary it.
slides.correction_move: Model one sentence, then prompt for a second sentence with one changed word or part.
slides.observation_note: Push for full oral language, not one-word answers.

content_payload.title: Close the Lesson

check_items.label: Which new sound did we learn today? How many spellings does it have?
Where did the cat sit? Is the cat sick? How do you know?

content_payload.notes_field: Keep the close brief, oral, and text-based.

slides.teacher_cue: Close with pattern recall, meaning from the reader, and one brief oral transfer sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students answer orally, refer back to the reader when needed, and produce one full sentence with lesson vocabulary.
slides.correction_move: Return to the reader, point to the relevant sentence, then model one full oral answer.
slides.observation_note: Watch for pattern recall, text-based answers, and whether the final oral sentence stays accurate and complete.

slides.teacher_cue: Show the sentence starter. Students write one full sentence that uses at least one lesson word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students write one complete sentence using at least one lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model one short sentence aloud, then have students write their own version.
slides.observation_note: Watch for accurate spelling of lesson words and a complete sentence frame.

content_payload.support_text: Say one final strong sentence using today's c and k focus.

slides.teacher_cue: Give me one more full sentence or idea using today's c and k focus before we finish.
slides.expected_response: Students give one final complete sentence or idea connected to the lesson focus.
slides.correction_move: If needed, model the start of a sentence and have students finish it clearly.
slides.observation_note: End with a strong oral response so the lesson closes on language and meaning.
